relationships.subject: Substance P
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings suggest that these neuropeptides play a non-essential role in pain, challenging the notion that the compensatory activities of Substance P and CGRPα account for the lack of strong pain phenotypes in animals carrying the gene for only one of the two neuropeptides.

relationships.subject: CGRPα
relationships.evidence_quote: Inhibiting CGRPα has shown positive effects in animal models of migraine, and several therapeutics that block CGRPα or its receptor are now approved for treating this condition

key_findings: Commentary on MacDonald et al.: Substance P/CGRPα double knockout mice show no change in responses to harmful stimuli.
Possible caveats: opposing spinal vs brain effects, developmental compensation, sex differences.
